conventions.convention: The Coxeter group W is finite; the coefficient field k has characteristic zero; Laurent parameters are indexed by odd-edge connected classes. The quadratic normalization is (T_s − v_[s])(T_s + v_[s]⁻¹) = 0.

The regular-trace pairing is B(x,y) = Tr(L_xy), distinct from the canonical coefficient-at-identity symmetrizing pairing. Its universal trace is defined by the diagonal sum in the specified standard basis; coefficient specialization carries its Gram determinant to the specialized determinant.

Formal deformation uses R = k[[h]], a finite free unital R-algebra, and a specified split semisimple reduction with finitely many matrix blocks of positive sizes. The formal branch allows any field k.

Determinant nonvanishing certifies semisimplicity, without asserting splitness. The determinant zero set is the exceptional set for this certificate, without an asserted equality with the nonsemisimple locus.
Finite direct summands include rank zero; a complete orthogonal idempotent family may be empty, and the formal matrix decomposition permits an empty block set when A = 0.

load_bearing.statement: Let k be a field, R = k[[h]], and A a unital R-algebra free of finite rank. A specified decomposition A/hA ≅ ∏ Mat_dλ(k), with finite index set and positive block sizes, lifts to an R-algebra isomorphism A ≅ ∏ Mat_dλ(R) whose reduction is the given decomposition.

For the finite-dimensional field specialization H = H_φ, nondegeneracy of B(x,y) = Tr_K(L_xy) implies that the left regular H-module is semisimple. This implication holds over every field; no converse is asserted.

For a field k, R = k[[h]] has residue field R/hR ≅ k, is an integral domain, and is complete and separated for the h-adic topology. Every finite free R-module is complete and separated coefficientwise, and Frac(R) is a field containing R injectively.

For finite W and characteristic-zero k, define the universal regular-trace Gram determinant D_W over R_k in the standard Hecke basis. For a ring homomorphism φ:R_k → K to a field, define H_φ = K ⊗ H_Rk and D_φ from its regular-trace Gram matrix; D_φ = φ(D_W).
Every finite complete orthogonal idempotent family in A/hA lifts to a finite complete orthogonal idempotent family in A, for a finite free unital k[[h]]-algebra A.
For n ≥ 0 and an idempotent R-linear map p:Rⁿ → Rⁿ over R = k[[h]], M = p(Rⁿ) is free of finite rank dim_k(M/hM), including M = 0.
For finite W over characteristic-zero k, D_W ≠ 0 and the Hecke algebra over Frac(R_k) is semisimple. Every field specialization φ with φ(D_W) ≠ 0 is semisimple. No splitness claim is made.

A finite free unital k[[h]]-algebra with specified split semisimple reduction ∏ Mat_dλ(k) has simple-module isomorphism classes in its special and generic fibers indexed by the same finite set, with dimensions dλ. Separately, regular-trace determinant nonvanishing certifies semisimplicity of characteristic-zero finite Hecke specializations.

concerns.concern: Verification 1.1 says, “The principal ideal is $Rp$ by [F5]”. Here R was fixed as Q[[h]], whereas the ideal is formed in R[X], so it is R[X]p. The preceding degree argument correctly treats polynomial multiples; the displayed notation incorrectly restricts them to constant multiples. F5 has the same ambiguous use of Rp in this context.

seams_checked.note: The canonical-trace definition and theorem give the coefficient-at-identity pairing with permutation Gram matrix under the same normalized quadratic relation. This batch correctly distinguishes that perfect symmetrizing pairing from regular trace, and its rank-one counterexample verifies the distinction directly. No semisimplicity implication is imported from the canonical trace.

The named planned seam has no current substantive citation to this batch in the consumer page or its listed items. The current centralizer supplier uses matrix-rank specialization, and the final theorem explicitly proves the equalities without generic semisimplicity. Consequently no claim about splitness, labels or specialized semisimplicity is imported or overstated.
